components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — beasts and hunting dogs, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.

example.hanzi: 爸爸小时候常常跟爷爷一起去打猎。
example.pinyin: bàba xiǎo shíhou chángcháng gēn yéye yìqǐ qù dǎliè.
example.english: When Dad was young, he often went hunting with Grandpa.
example.fact: Long before the bow and arrow, ancient hunters used a tool called an atlatl — a spear-thrower with a notched handle — to nearly double the speed and range of a thrown dart. Some atlatl-launched projectiles could travel over 100 meters, and the technology appears independently in hunting cultures across the Americas, Australia, and Europe going back at least 20,000 years.

examples.hanzi: 他们一家人周末去森林里打猎。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yī jiā rén zhōumò qù sēnlín lǐ dǎliè.
examples.english: The family goes hunting in the forest on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 现在很多地方不允许随便打猎。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō dìfang bù yǔnxǔ suíbiàn dǎliè.
examples.english: Nowadays, hunting is not allowed everywhere without permission.

components.note: 氵 (water) — crossing a river; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
度 (dù) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 镀 dù.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 他们乘小船渡过了那条河。
example.pinyin: tāmen chéng xiǎochuán dùguò le nà tiáo hé.
example.english: They crossed that river by small boat.
example.fact: In 49 BC, Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon River, a shallow stream in northern Italy, defying Roman law that forbade a general from bringing troops into Italy proper. The crossing triggered a civil war and gave rise to the modern idiom "crossing the Rubicon" for passing a point of no return.

examples.hanzi: 我们终于渡过了最困难的时期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú dùguò le zuì kùnnan de shíqī.
examples.english: We finally got through the most difficult period.

examples.hanzi: 他在国外渡过了愉快的童年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guówài dùguò le yúkuài de tóngnián.
examples.english: He spent a happy childhood abroad.

meanings: (of a liquid or gas) to leak

components.note: 氵 (water) — leaking liquid; also in 漏 leak, 流 flow.
世 (shì) is only a loose sound clue for xiè.
氵 (water) — water leaking through; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
屚 (lòu) — rain (雨) under a roof (尸): a leaking roof. It gives the sound and also sounds out 陋 lòu.

example.hanzi: 那家工厂发生了化学品泄漏事故。
example.pinyin: nà jiā gōngchǎng fāshēng le huàxuépǐn xièlòu shìgù.
example.english: That factory had a chemical leak accident.
example.fact: The 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster in the Gulf of Mexico released an estimated 4.9 million barrels of oil over 87 days before the well was capped, making it the largest accidental marine oil spill in history. Engineers eventually stopped the leak using a specially designed capping stack lowered more than a mile to the seafloor.

examples.hanzi: 这份机密文件被人泄漏给了媒体。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn jīmì wénjiàn bèi rén xièlòu gěi le méitǐ.
examples.english: This confidential document was leaked to the media.

examples.hanzi: 煤气泄漏时，要马上开窗通风。
examples.pinyin: Méiqì xièlòu shí, yào mǎshàng kāichuāng tōngfēng.
examples.english: When there is a gas leak, open the windows for ventilation immediately.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 怪不得今天这么冷，原来下雪了。
example.pinyin: guàibude jīntiān zhème lěng, yuánlái xià xuě le.
example.english: No wonder it's so cold today — it's actually snowing.
example.fact: Snow forms only when the atmosphere is cold enough for ice crystals to grow around microscopic dust or pollen particles high in the clouds; if the air near the ground warms even slightly above freezing on the way down, the flakes melt into rain instead. Each snowflake's six-sided symmetry comes from the hexagonal way water molecules bond as they freeze.

examples.hanzi: 怪不得他不高兴，原来你忘了他的生日。
examples.pinyin: Guàibude tā bù gāoxìng, yuánlái nǐ wàng le tā de shēngrì.
examples.english: No wonder he's unhappy, you forgot his birthday.

examples.hanzi: 他在国外住了十年，怪不得英语这么好。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guówài zhù le shí nián, guàibude Yīngyǔ zhème hǎo.
examples.english: He lived abroad for ten years, so no wonder his English is so good.

components.note: 阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — land and hills, as in 院, 阳, 队. The right part is a simplification with no sound clue.
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 他退伍前是海军陆战队的一名军官。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ qián shì hǎijūn lùzhànduì de yì míng jūnguān.
example.english: Before he left the service, he was an officer in the marine corps.
example.fact: The United States Marine Corps traces its founding to November 10, 1775, when the Second Continental Congress authorized two battalions of Marines to serve aboard Navy ships. That founding date is still celebrated annually as the Marine Corps' birthday, making it one of the oldest continuously operating military branches in the country.

examples.hanzi: 他在海军陆战队服役了四年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hǎijūn lùzhànduì fúyì le sì nián.
examples.english: He served four years in the Marine Corps.

examples.hanzi: 陆战队员在海滩上进行了登陆训练。
examples.pinyin: Lùzhànduì yuán zài hǎitān shàng jìnxíng le dēnglù xùnliàn.
examples.english: The marines carried out landing drills on the beach.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洗 is to wash.
先 (xiān) — near sound — 洗 is xǐ; 先 also sounds out 选 xuǎn.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 吃饭前记得洗手。
example.pinyin: chīfàn qián jìde xǐshǒu.
example.english: Remember to wash your hands before eating.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that maternity ward deaths from childbed fever dropped sharply after he required doctors to wash their hands with a chlorinated lime solution between autopsies and patient exams. His findings were ridiculed by the medical establishment of the time, and it took decades — after germ theory was widely accepted — for handwashing to become standard practice.

examples.hanzi: 洗手要用肥皂搓二十秒。
examples.pinyin: Xǐshǒu yào yòng féizào cuō èrshí miǎo.
examples.english: When washing your hands, scrub with soap for twenty seconds.

examples.hanzi: 请问，洗手间在哪里？我想洗手。
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, xǐshǒujiān zài nǎlǐ? Wǒ xiǎng xǐshǒu.
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom? I want to wash my hands.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.

example.hanzi: 这次歌唱比赛先进行海选，再决出决赛选手。
example.pinyin: zhè cì gēchàng bǐsài xiān jìnxíng hǎixuǎn, zài juéchū juésài xuǎnshǒu.
example.english: This singing competition starts with an open audition before the finalists are decided.
example.fact: Many corals and reef fish reproduce through mass spawning events, releasing millions of eggs and sperm into the water at once during a single synchronized night each year, often timed to the lunar cycle. Broadcasting so many gametes into the open ocean compensates for the fact that only a tiny fraction will ever meet and survive.

examples.hanzi: 这档节目的海选吸引了上万人报名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dàng jiémù de hǎixuǎn xīyǐn le shàng wàn rén bàomíng.
examples.english: The open audition for this show attracted tens of thousands of sign-ups.

examples.hanzi: 她在海选中唱了一首老歌，评委都很喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hǎixuǎn zhōng chàng le yī shǒu lǎo gē, píngwěi dōu hěn xǐhuan.
examples.english: She sang an old song at the open audition, and the judges loved it.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 最近他的行为有些失常。
example.pinyin: zuìjìn tā de xíngwéi yǒuxiē shīcháng.
example.english: His behavior has been a bit abnormal lately.
example.fact: El Niño is an irregular, naturally occurring disruption of normal ocean-atmosphere patterns in which surface waters in the eastern Pacific warm several degrees above average, altering weather worldwide. It recurs every two to seven years without a fixed schedule, which is part of why forecasting its onset and strength remains genuinely difficult even with modern satellite data.

examples.hanzi: 他今天考试时发挥失常，成绩很差。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān kǎoshì shí fāhuī shīcháng, chéngjì hěn chà.
examples.english: He performed below par in the exam today and his score was poor.

examples.hanzi: 机器的运转有些失常，需要检修。
examples.pinyin: Jīqì de yùnzhuàn yǒuxiē shīcháng, xūyào jiǎnxiū.
examples.english: The machine is running abnormally and needs servicing.

components.note: 音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去百老汇看了一场音乐剧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōumò qù Bǎilǎohuì kàn le yì chǎng yīnyuèjù.
example.english: We went to see a musical on Broadway this weekend.
example.fact: "The Phantom of the Opera" opened on Broadway in 1988 and ran continuously for 35 years before closing in April 2023, racking up more than 13,500 performances — the longest run in Broadway history. Its original production reportedly grossed over one billion dollars in New York alone.

examples.hanzi: 《猫》是一部很受欢迎的音乐剧。
examples.pinyin: 《Māo》 shì yī bù hěn shòu huānyíng de yīnyuèjù.
examples.english: Cats is a very popular musical.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就想演音乐剧。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng yǎn yīnyuèjù.
examples.english: She has wanted to act in musicals since childhood.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.hanzi: 新技术大大推进了这个项目的进度。
example.pinyin: xīn jìshù dàdà tuījìn le zhège xiàngmù de jìndù.
example.english: The new technology greatly advanced the project's progress.
example.fact: A rocket engine propels itself forward by Newton's third law: expelling exhaust gas backward at high speed generates an equal and opposite thrust forward, working even in the vacuum of space where there's no air to push against. The Saturn V rocket's first stage burned roughly 15 tons of fuel per second to generate enough thrust to lift itself off the launch pad.

examples.hanzi: 新政策正在逐步推进。
examples.pinyin: Xīn zhèngcè zhèngzài zhúbù tuījìn.
examples.english: The new policy is being pushed forward step by step.

examples.hanzi: 火箭靠强大的动力推进。
examples.pinyin: Huǒjiàn kào qiángdà de dònglì tuījìn.
examples.english: The rocket is propelled by powerful engines.

components.note: 鬲 (cooking cauldron) — steam rising from a pot, things heating and blending; 虫 (chóng) is only a loose sound clue.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 太阳出来后，雪很快就融化了。
example.pinyin: tàiyáng chūlái hòu, xuě hěn kuài jiù rónghuà le.
example.english: After the sun came out, the snow melted quickly.
example.fact: Arctic sea ice has been shrinking at a rate of roughly 13 percent per decade since satellite records began in 1979, with the region's summer minimum extent now less than half of what it was forty years ago. Because darker open ocean water absorbs more sunlight than reflective ice, the melting accelerates further warming in a feedback loop scientists call Arctic amplification.

examples.hanzi: 冰淇淋放久了会融化。
examples.pinyin: Bīngqílín fàng jiǔ le huì rónghuà.
examples.english: Ice cream melts if left out too long.

examples.hanzi: 春天来了，河面上的冰开始融化。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, hémiàn shàng de bīng kāishǐ rónghuà.
examples.english: Spring has come and the ice on the river is starting to melt.

components.note: 予 (give) — 幻 is 予 written reversed — giving turned around, an illusion.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢看科幻电影。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan kàn kēhuàn diànyǐng.
example.english: He likes watching sci-fi movies.
example.fact: 幻 appears in 科幻 (sci-fi), 幻想 (fantasy), 幻觉 (hallucination), 梦幻 (dreamy). 幻灯片 is a slide, e.g. in a presentation.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都喜欢看幻想故事。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu xǐhuan kàn huànxiǎng gùshi.
examples.english: Children all enjoy fantasy stories.

examples.hanzi: 她以为那只是一个幻觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐwéi nà zhǐ shì yí ge huànjué.
examples.english: She thought it was only an illusion.

components.note: 川 (river) — three lines of flowing water; used for rivers and streams, as in 四川 Sichuan, 山川 mountains and rivers.

example.hanzi: 四川菜很辣。
example.pinyin: Sìchuān cài hěn là.
example.english: Sichuan food is very spicy.
example.fact: 川 is also the short name for Sichuan, 'the four rivers'. 川菜 is Sichuan cuisine, and 川 appears in 山川 (mountains and rivers).

examples.hanzi: 我们周末要去四川旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò yào qù Sìchuān lǚyóu.
examples.english: We are going to Sichuan this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 山川河流都很美。
examples.pinyin: Shānchuān héliú dōu hěn měi.
examples.english: The mountains and rivers are all beautiful.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 捞 is scooping something out of water.
劳 (láo) — close sound: 捞 lāo. 劳 also sounds out 涝 lào and 唠 lào.

example.hanzi: 他把掉进水里的手机捞了出来。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ diào jìn shuǐ lǐ de shǒujī lāo le chūlái.
example.english: He fished the phone out of the water.
example.fact: 捞 is colloquial: 打捞 (salvage), 捞一把 (to grab a profit), 捞钱 (to make money, often dishonestly).

examples.hanzi: 他拿着网把鱼捞了上来。
examples.pinyin: Tā ná zhe wǎng bǎ yú lāo le shànglái.
examples.english: He used a net to scoop the fish out.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我从火锅里捞出一块肉。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ cóng huǒguō lǐ lāo chū yí kuài ròu.
examples.english: Please fish a piece of meat out of the soup for me.

components.note: 门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 有人在门外等你。
example.pinyin: yǒu rén zài ménwài děng nǐ.
example.english: Someone is waiting for you outside the door.
example.fact: The oldest known wooden door in Europe, unearthed near Zurich, Switzerland, dates back to around 3400 BC and was preserved for millennia in waterlogged lakeside soil. It still has visible tool marks from its construction, offering rare direct evidence of Neolithic carpentry.

examples.hanzi: 他在门外敲了半天门。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài ménwài qiāo le bàntiān mén.
examples.english: He knocked on the door outside for a long time.

examples.hanzi: 门外停着一辆很旧的自行车。
examples.pinyin: Ménwài tíng zhe yī liàng hěn jiù de zìxíngchē.
examples.english: A very old bicycle is parked outside the door.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 前方路况不好，请小心驾驶。
example.pinyin: qiánfāng lùkuàng bù hǎo, qǐng xiǎoxīn jiàshǐ.
example.english: Road conditions ahead are poor, please drive carefully.
example.fact: Modern car radar can detect obstacles hundreds of meters ahead by bouncing radio waves off objects and timing their return, the same basic principle used in the earliest air-defense radar systems developed in Britain in the 1930s. Today's automatic emergency braking systems use this to react to a hazard ahead in a fraction of a second — far faster than human reflexes allow.

examples.hanzi: 前方两百米有一个红绿灯。
examples.pinyin: Qiánfāng liǎng bǎi mǐ yǒu yī gè hónglǜdēng.
examples.english: There is a traffic light two hundred meters ahead.

examples.hanzi: 我们要朝着前方的目标努力。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cháo zhe qiánfāng de mùbiāo nǔlì.
examples.english: We should work toward the goal ahead.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
疒 (illness) — marks wounds and ailments, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain; 疤 is a scar.
巴 (bā) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 吧 ba, 爸 bà and 芭 bā.

example.hanzi: 他手臂上有一道很深的伤疤。
example.pinyin: tā shǒubì shàng yǒu yì dào hěn shēn de shāngbā.
example.english: There's a deep scar on his arm.
example.fact: Scar tissue forms when the skin's collagen fibers, which normally weave in a random basket-like pattern, instead line up in parallel bundles during rapid wound repair. That different arrangement is why scars look and feel distinct from surrounding skin and never regrow hair follicles or sweat glands.

examples.hanzi: 这道伤疤是我小时候摔倒留下的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào shāngbā shì wǒ xiǎoshíhou shuāidǎo liúxià de.
examples.english: This scar came from a fall when I was little.

examples.hanzi: 伤口好了以后，会留下一道浅浅的伤疤。
examples.pinyin: Shāngkǒu hǎo le yǐhòu, huì liúxià yī dào qiǎnqiǎn de shāngbā.
examples.english: After the wound heals, a faint scar will remain.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — water creatures, as in 鲨 shark, 鲜 fresh; 鳄 is the crocodile.
咢 (è) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 愕 è and 腭 è.
鱼 (fish) — a picture of a fish: head on top, scaly body 田, tail 一. As a radical (鱼) it marks fish, as in 鲨, 鲜.

example.hanzi: 河里有一条鳄鱼在晒太阳。
example.pinyin: hé lǐ yǒu yì tiáo èyú zài shài tàiyáng.
example.english: There's a crocodile sunbathing in the river.
example.fact: American alligators can go through as many as 3,000 to 4,000 teeth over a lifetime, constantly replacing worn or lost ones with new teeth growing in beneath the old — a capability scientists have studied for clues about regenerating human dental tissue. Their bite force, meanwhile, is among the strongest measured in any living animal, while the muscles that open their jaws are comparatively weak.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里的鳄鱼张开了大嘴。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de èyú zhāng kāi le dà zuǐ.
examples.english: The crocodile in the zoo opened its big mouth.

examples.hanzi: 这个钱包是用鳄鱼皮做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qiánbāo shì yòng èyú pí zuò de.
examples.english: This wallet is made of crocodile skin.

components.note: 皮 (skin) — a hand 又 stripping hide from an animal; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī, 坡 pō and 玻 bō.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.

example.hanzi: 他的皮带上有一个金属扣。
example.pinyin: tā de pídài shàng yǒu yí gè jīnshǔ kòu.
example.english: There's a metal buckle on his belt.
example.fact: During the early Industrial Revolution, factories often ran on a single large steam engine that drove one central rotating shaft running the length of the building, with long leather belts looping down to power each individual machine. This "belt and pulley" system meant that if the main engine stopped, every machine in the factory stopped with it.

examples.hanzi: 这条裤子太松了，要系一条皮带。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài sōng le, yào jì yī tiáo pídài.
examples.english: These trousers are too loose, so I need a belt.

examples.hanzi: 传送皮带坏了，机器停了下来。
examples.pinyin: Chuánsòng pídài huài le, jīqì tíng le xiàlái.
examples.english: The conveyor belt broke and the machine stopped.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 出门时她总是随身带着一把雨伞。
example.pinyin: chūmén shí tā zǒngshì suíshēn dài zhe yì bǎ yǔsǎn.
example.english: She always carries an umbrella with her when she goes out.
example.fact: Sony's 1979 Walkman was one of the first devices to make truly personal, portable audio possible, letting people carry music with them wherever they went instead of being tied to a stationary stereo. It sold over 200 million units worldwide across its various models before production finally ended in 2010.

examples.hanzi: 请随身携带你的身份证。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng suíshēn xiédài nǐ de shēnfènzhèng.
examples.english: Please carry your ID with you.

examples.hanzi: 飞机上的随身行李不能超过七公斤。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī shàng de suíshēn xíngli bù néng chāoguò qī gōngjīn.
examples.english: Carry-on luggage on the plane cannot exceed seven kilograms.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 跨 is striding or stepping over.
夸 (kuā) — close sound: 跨 kuà. 夸 also sounds out 垮 kuǎ and 挎 kuà.

example.hanzi: 他跨过了那条小河。
example.pinyin: Tā kuàguò le nà tiáo xiǎo hé.
example.english: He stepped over the little stream.
example.fact: 跨 now spans 'across' in many modern words: 跨国 (multinational), 跨境 (cross-border), 跨年 (to ring in the New Year) and 跨界 (crossover).

examples.hanzi: 这座大桥横跨在长江上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò dàqiáo héngkuà zài Chángjiāng shàng.
examples.english: This big bridge spans the Yangtze River.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司有很多跨国客户。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěn duō kuàguó kèhù.
examples.english: This company has many multinational clients.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 裙 is a skirt.
君 (jūn) — near sound — 裙 is qún; 君 also sounds out 群 qún.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条红裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo hóng qúnzi.
example.english: She is wearing a red skirt.
example.fact: The measure word is 条: 一条裙子. 连衣裙 is a dress. 裙带关系 ('skirt-belt relationship') means nepotism.

examples.hanzi: 夏天她喜欢穿连衣裙。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān tā xǐhuan chuān liányīqún.
examples.english: In summer she likes to wear dresses.

examples.hanzi: 这条裙子的颜色很好看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi de yánsè hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: The color of this skirt is very pretty.

components.note: 吉 (jí) — lucky; as a part it sounds out 结 jié and 洁 jié.
米 (rice) — a picture of grains of rice divided by a line; as a radical it marks grain foods, as in 粉 powder, 粮 grain, 糖 sugar.

example.hanzi: 我的邻居吉米每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: wǒ de línjū Jímǐ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: My neighbor Jimmy goes running every morning.
example.fact: Jimmy Carter, the 39th President of the United States, left office in 1981 but went on to found the Carter Center and spend decades on humanitarian work, including election monitoring and public health campaigns in dozens of countries. In 2002, he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for those post-presidency efforts.

examples.hanzi: 吉米是我儿子的同班同学。
examples.pinyin: Jímǐ shì wǒ érzi de tóngbān tóngxué.
examples.english: Jimmy is my son's classmate.

examples.hanzi: 吉米昨天给我打了个电话，邀请我去他家。
examples.pinyin: Jímǐ zuótiān gěi wǒ dǎ le gè diànhuà, yāoqǐng wǒ qù tā jiā.
examples.english: Jimmy called me yesterday and invited me to his house.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — hands lifting an offering: to present respectfully. 奉 also sounds out 捧 pěng and 俸 fèng.
犬 (dog) — a sacrifice was offered with a dog, hence 献 is to present or offer; the left side is a simplified stand-in.

example.hanzi: 她把一生都奉献给了科学研究。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ yìshēng dōu fèngxiàn gěi le kēxué yánjiū.
example.english: She dedicated her whole life to scientific research.
example.fact: Marie Curie donated the prize money from her first Nobel Prize to scientific research rather than keeping it, and she and her husband deliberately chose not to patent their process for isolating radium so other scientists could use it freely. She died in 1934 of aplastic anemia, almost certainly caused by decades of unprotected exposure to the radioactive materials she studied.

examples.hanzi: 他为这个社区奉献了自己的时间和精力。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi zhège shèqū fèngxiàn le zìjǐ de shíjiān hé jīnglì.
examples.english: He dedicated his time and energy to this community.

examples.hanzi: 医生们的无私奉献让人感动。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēngmen de wúsī fèngxiàn ràng rén gǎndòng.
examples.english: The doctors' selfless dedication is moving.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 means strength, here force — 劫 is to seize by force; compare 办, 动, 努.
去 (qù) — the sound has drifted — 劫 is jié, so 去 is only a rough clue.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 那架飞机在飞行途中被劫持了。
example.pinyin: nà jià fēijī zài fēixíng túzhōng bèi jiéchí le.
example.english: That plane was hijacked mid-flight.
example.fact: In November 1971, a man using the alias D.B. Cooper hijacked a Boeing 727, demanded $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted out of the plane over the Pacific Northwest — and was never identified or found. The FBI officially closed the unsolved case in 2016, and only a small portion of the ransom cash, found years later along a riverbank, was ever recovered.

examples.hanzi: 歹徒劫持了一辆公共汽车。
examples.pinyin: Dǎitú jiéchí le yī liàng gōnggòng qìchē.
examples.english: The criminals hijacked a bus.

examples.hanzi: 警察成功解救了被劫持的人质。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá chénggōng jiějiù le bèi jiéchí de rénzhì.
examples.english: The police successfully rescued the hostages who had been abducted.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.hanzi: 图书馆是一个安静的学习场所。
example.pinyin: túshūguǎn shì yí gè ānjìng de xuéxí chǎngsuǒ.
example.english: The library is a quiet place to study.
example.fact: Before satellite navigation, pinpointing an exact location at sea depended on knowing accurate time: British clockmaker John Harrison spent decades in the 1700s perfecting a marine chronometer precise enough to determine longitude by comparing local noon to a fixed reference time, finally solving a problem that had cost thousands of sailors' lives to shipwreck.

examples.hanzi: 公共场所请不要大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ qǐng bù yào dàshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: Please do not talk loudly in public places.

examples.hanzi: 这里是举行婚礼的好场所。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ shì jǔxíng hūnlǐ de hǎo chǎngsuǒ.
examples.english: This is a good venue for a wedding.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 换 is to swap with the hands.
奂 (huàn) — same sound — 换 is huàn, like 奂; 奂 also sounds out 唤 huàn.

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以把文件转换成不同的格式。
example.pinyin: zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ bǎ wénjiàn zhuǎnhuàn chéng bùtóng de géshì.
example.english: This software can convert files into different formats.
example.fact: Hoover Dam converts the gravitational potential energy of water held behind it into electricity by letting the water fall roughly 180 meters through turbines, spinning generators that once supplied enough power for the entire Las Vegas region. Hydropower remains one of the most efficient energy conversion methods known, often exceeding 90 percent efficiency from moving water to electrical output.

examples.hanzi: 你可以把人民币转换成美元。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ rénmínbì zhuǎnhuàn chéng měiyuán.
examples.english: You can convert RMB into US dollars.

examples.hanzi: 换了新工作后，他需要时间转换角色。
examples.pinyin: Huàn le xīn gōngzuò hòu, tā xūyào shíjiān zhuǎnhuàn juésè.
examples.english: After changing jobs, he needs time to adjust to his new role.

components.note: 礻 (spirit, from 示) — marks ritual and spirits, as in 神 god, 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; 祖 is an ancestor, honoured at the altar.
且 (qiě) hints at the sound: 祖 zǔ is close to 组 zǔ, 阻 zǔ and 租 zū.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 他常常给远在祖国的家人写信。
example.pinyin: tā chángcháng gěi yuǎn zài zǔguó de jiārén xiě xìn.
example.english: He often writes letters to his family far away in his homeland.
example.fact: Russia, often called the "motherland" in its own patriotic tradition, is the largest country on Earth by land area, spanning eleven time zones and covering more than one-eighth of the planet's inhabited land. It stretches so far that when it's morning in its westernmost city, it's already nighttime on its eastern edge.

examples.hanzi: 无论走到哪里，他都想念祖国。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn zǒu dào nǎlǐ, tā dōu xiǎngniàn zǔguó.
examples.english: Wherever he goes, he misses his motherland.

examples.hanzi: 运动员们为祖国赢得了荣誉。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòngyuánmen wèi zǔguó yíngdé le róngyù.
examples.english: The athletes won honor for their country.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.

example.hanzi: 罗马军团曾征服了大片欧洲土地。
example.pinyin: Luómǎ jūntuán céng zhēngfú le dà piàn Ōuzhōu tǔdì.
example.english: Roman legions once conquered vast stretches of European territory.
example.fact: A standard Roman legion in the early imperial period numbered around 5,000 soldiers, organized into ten cohorts and further divided into smaller units called centuries — despite the name, typically about 80 men rather than a literal 100. At its height, the Roman Empire maintained roughly 30 legions simultaneously stationed across three continents.

examples.hanzi: 这支军团由五千名士兵组成。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī jūntuán yóu wǔqiān míng shìbīng zǔchéng.
examples.english: This legion is made up of five thousand soldiers.

examples.hanzi: 游戏里的玩家可以加入不同的军团。
examples.pinyin: Yóuxì lǐ de wánjiā kěyǐ jiārù bùtóng de jūntuán.
examples.english: Players in the game can join different legions.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
月 (moon) — moonlight, clear and bright; also in 明 bright.
良 (liáng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 浪 làng, 狼 láng and 郎 láng.

example.hanzi: 布朗先生是这所学校的新校长。
example.pinyin: Bùlǎng xiānsheng shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào de xīn xiàozhǎng.
example.english: Mr. Brown is the new principal of this school.
example.fact: In 1827, Scottish botanist Robert Brown observed pollen grains suspended in water jittering constantly under his microscope for no apparent reason. That erratic motion, later named Brownian motion after him, wasn't fully explained until 1905, when Albert Einstein showed it was caused by countless collisions with individual water molecules — providing some of the first solid evidence that atoms and molecules actually exist.

examples.hanzi: 布朗太太每天早上都给花浇水。
examples.pinyin: Bùlǎng tàitai měitiān zǎoshang dōu gěi huā jiāoshuǐ.
examples.english: Mrs. Brown waters the flowers every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我的同事布朗说他下周要出差。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì Bùlǎng shuō tā xià zhōu yào chūchāi.
examples.english: My colleague Brown said he's going on a business trip next week.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他这次来纯粹是为了公事。
example.pinyin: tā zhè cì lái chúncuì shì wèile gōngshì.
example.english: This time he came purely for official business.
example.fact: China's imperial civil service examination system, which selected government officials based on merit rather than birth, was formally established during the Sui and Tang dynasties around the 7th century and lasted until it was abolished in 1905. It's considered one of the earliest large-scale meritocratic bureaucracies in world history, and versions of its written-exam model influenced civil service systems in Europe and beyond.

examples.hanzi: 我们先谈公事，再聊私事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān tán gōngshì, zài liáo sīshì.
examples.english: Let's discuss business first and then personal matters.

examples.hanzi: 他因为公事去了一趟上海。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngshì qù le yī tàng Shànghǎi.
examples.english: He made a trip to Shanghai on business.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这是一个非常感人的故事。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yí gè fēicháng gǎnrén de gùshi.
example.english: This is a very touching story.
example.fact: Oxytocin, sometimes nicknamed the "bonding hormone," is released in the brain during moments of physical closeness like hugging or reunion, and it appears to strengthen feelings of trust and attachment between people. Studies have found oxytocin levels rise not just during physical contact but even while watching emotionally moving scenes, such as a tearful reunion in a film.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的结尾特别感人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéwěi tèbié gǎnrén.
examples.english: The ending of this movie is especially touching.

examples.hanzi: 他们之间有一段感人的友情。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu yī duàn gǎnrén de yǒuqíng.
examples.english: There is a moving friendship between them.

components.note: 土 (earth) — banking up soil around plants; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
咅 (pōu) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 陪 péi and 赔 péi.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and teaching: 说, 请, 课; 训 is instruction.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 shares its part with 顺 shùn.

example.hanzi: 新员工要先完成一周的培训。
example.pinyin: xīn yuángōng yào xiān wánchéng yì zhōu de péixùn.
example.english: New employees must first complete a week of training.
example.fact: Medieval craft guilds in Europe typically required apprentices to train under a master for around seven years before they could even attempt the "masterpiece" exam needed to become a master craftsman themselves. The system was so central to how skills were passed on that many guilds tightly controlled how many apprentices any master could train at once, to protect the value of the trade.

examples.hanzi: 公司给我们安排了英语培训。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī gěi wǒmen ānpái le Yīngyǔ péixùn.
examples.english: The company arranged English training for us.

examples.hanzi: 她正在培训班里学习做蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài péixùn bān lǐ xuéxí zuò dàngāo.
examples.english: She is learning to bake cakes in a training course.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 队员们互相传球，配合得很好。
example.pinyin: duìyuánmen hùxiāng chuánqiú, pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: The teammates passed the ball to each other and worked together well.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by physical education teacher James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony and used a soccer ball, since basketballs themselves didn't exist yet. Because the baskets had solid bottoms at first, someone had to climb a ladder to retrieve the ball after every score until the open-bottomed hoop was introduced years later.

examples.hanzi: 他及时传球给了站在前面的队友。
examples.pinyin: Tā jíshí chuánqiú gěi le zhàn zài qiánmiàn de duìyǒu.
examples.english: He passed the ball in time to the teammate standing in front.

examples.hanzi: 这位球员的传球非常精准。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi qiúyuán de chuánqiú fēicháng jīngzhǔn.
examples.english: This player's passing is very accurate.

components.note: 亠 (lid) — the top stroke group, as in 市 and 交. The sound-borrowed number; no meaning link. Memory aid: a lid on top of 八 (eight) ends up as six.
八 (eight) — the bottom part, as in 分 divide. Same shape as 'eight' but the number 六 does not come from it; use it as a visual memory aid.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 我们六点在门口见面吧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen liùdiǎn zài ménkǒu jiànmiàn ba.
example.english: Let's meet at the entrance at six o'clock.
example.fact: Before the adoption of standardized time zones, every town commonly kept its own local solar time, so "six o'clock" could differ by minutes between neighboring cities — a serious problem once railway schedules connected them. The 1884 International Meridian Conference fixed this by establishing 24 worldwide time zones measured from the Greenwich meridian, the system still in use today.

examples.hanzi: 每天早上六点，闹钟准时响起。
examples.pinyin: Měitiān zǎoshang liù diǎn, nàozhōng zhǔnshí xiǎngqǐ.
examples.english: Every morning at six, the alarm goes off on time.

examples.hanzi: 现在是六点半，不是六点。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì liù diǎn bàn, bù shì liù diǎn.
examples.english: It's six thirty now, not six.

components.note: 饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱; 馆 is an inn or restaurant, a place that serves food.
官 (guān) sounds exactly like 馆 apart from tone; also in 管 guǎn.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去图书馆。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù túshūguǎn.
example.english: We're going to the library at the weekend.
example.fact: 馆 is used as a suffix for public places: 图书馆 (library), 博物馆 (museum), 饭馆 (restaurant), 宾馆 (hotel). 下馆子 means 'to eat out'.

examples.hanzi: 我们明天去博物馆参观。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān qù bówùguǎn cānguān.
examples.english: Tomorrow we are going to visit the museum.

examples.hanzi: 楼下新开了一家小餐馆。
examples.pinyin: Lóuxià xīn kāi le yì jiā xiǎo cānguǎn.
examples.english: A small restaurant has newly opened downstairs.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嗷 imitates wailing or howling.
敖 (áo) — same sound: 嗷 áo. 敖 also sounds out 熬 áo and 傲 ào.

example.hanzi: 小狗饿得嗷嗷叫。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu è de áoáo jiào.
example.english: The puppy is whimpering with hunger.
example.fact: 嗷 imitates crying. 嗷嗷待哺 (like hungry nestlings waiting to be fed) is an idiom for people in desperate need.

examples.hanzi: 狼在山上嗷嗷地叫。
examples.pinyin: Láng zài shān shàng áo'áo de jiào.
examples.english: The wolf is howling on the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 孩子嗷的一声哭了起来。
examples.pinyin: Háizi áo de yì shēng kū le qǐlái.
examples.english: The child burst into a wail.

components.note: 衣 (clothes) — a family: 表 outside, 袋 bag, 装 dress. 裔 first meant the hem of a robe; far from the body, hence far descendants (后裔).
冏 (window; bright) — the lower part; the dictionary calls it a meaning part. Memory aid: the hem trails down, like descendants far from the ancestors.

example.hanzi: 他是华裔美国人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì huáyì Měiguórén.
example.english: He is an American of Chinese descent.
example.fact: 裔 appears in 华裔 (a foreign national of Chinese descent), 后裔 (descendants), 亚裔 (Asian-descent) and 非裔 (African-descent). 华侨 refers to Chinese citizens living abroad.

examples.hanzi: 他的祖父是华裔，住在美国。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zǔfù shì huáyì, zhù zài Měiguó.
examples.english: His grandfather is of Chinese descent and lives in America.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家是一位韩裔美国人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā shì yí wèi Hányì Měiguórén.
examples.english: This writer is a Korean American.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 消防员及时解救了被困的孩子。
example.pinyin: xiāofángyuán jíshí jiějiù le bèi kùn de háizi.
example.english: The firefighters rescued the trapped child in time.
example.fact: In 2010, 33 Chilean miners survived 69 days trapped nearly 700 meters underground after a collapse at the San José mine, communicating with rescuers through a narrow borehole before all being pulled to the surface one by one in a specially built capsule named Fénix 2. The rescue was broadcast live and watched by an estimated one billion people worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 警察解救了被绑架的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá jiějiù le bèi bǎngjià de háizi.
examples.english: The police rescued the kidnapped child.

examples.hanzi: 你的建议解救了我们的危机。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de jiànyì jiějiù le wǒmen de wēijī.
examples.english: Your advice saved us from the crisis.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这架航班将飞往东京。
example.pinyin: zhè jià hángbān jiāng fēiwǎng Dōngjīng.
example.english: This flight will fly to Tokyo.
example.fact: The longest nonstop commercial flight in the world, Singapore Airlines' route from Singapore to New York, covers roughly 15,300 kilometers and takes about 18 hours in the air. Because ultra-long-haul flights like this carry so much fuel, airlines must carefully calculate weight trade-offs between fuel, passengers, and cargo before the plane can even take off.

examples.hanzi: 下一班飞往上海的飞机几点起飞？
examples.pinyin: Xià yī bān fēiwǎng Shànghǎi de fēijī jǐ diǎn qǐfēi?
examples.english: What time does the next flight to Shanghai take off?

examples.hanzi: 候鸟每年冬天都会飞往南方。
examples.pinyin: Hòuniǎo měinián dōngtiān dōu huì fēiwǎng nánfāng.
examples.english: Migratory birds fly south every winter.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 碎 is to smash into bits.
卒 (zú) hints at the sound: 碎 suì is close to 醉 zuì and 翠 cuì.

example.hanzi: 花瓶不小心被打碎了。
example.pinyin: huāpíng bù xiǎoxīn bèi dǎsuì le.
example.english: The vase was accidentally smashed.
example.fact: Tempered glass, used in car windows and phone screens, is manufactured by rapidly cooling the surface of hot glass while the interior cools more slowly, locking in internal stresses. When that engineered stress is finally broken, the glass shatters all at once into small, relatively blunt pebble-like pieces rather than sharp shards, which is why it's considered safer than ordinary glass.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不小心打碎了一个杯子。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bù xiǎoxīn dǎsuì le yī gè bēizi.
examples.english: The child accidentally smashed a cup.

examples.hanzi: 球打碎了邻居家的窗户。
examples.pinyin: Qiú dǎsuì le línjū jiā de chuānghu.
examples.english: The ball broke the neighbor's window.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.

example.hanzi: 她学习柔道是为了自卫。
example.pinyin: tā xuéxí Róudào shì wèile zìwèi.
example.english: She's learning judo for self-defense.
example.fact: A skunk's primary self-defense mechanism is a foul-smelling musk sprayed from glands near its tail, which it can aim accurately at a threat's face from as far as three meters away. Skunks typically give a warning display — stamping their feet and arching their back — before spraying, since they only carry enough musk for a few uses before needing time to replenish it.

examples.hanzi: 遇到危险时，你有权自卫。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào wēixiǎn shí, nǐ yǒu quán zìwèi.
examples.english: When in danger, you have the right to defend yourself.

examples.hanzi: 法律允许人们正当自卫。
examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ yǔnxǔ rénmen zhèngdàng zìwèi.
examples.english: The law allows people to act in legitimate self-defense.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 这条小路通向山顶。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo xiǎolù tōngxiàng shāndǐng.
example.english: This trail leads to the mountaintop.
example.fact: At its height, the Roman road network stretched more than 400,000 kilometers, with about 80,000 kilometers paved, connecting the empire from Britain to the Middle East. Well-built Roman roads used layered foundations of gravel and stone and were engineered with a slight curve to shed rainwater, a design so effective that some sections are still visible today.

examples.hanzi: 这条大路通向市中心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dàlù tōngxiàng shì zhōngxīn.
examples.english: This main road leads to the city center.

examples.hanzi: 努力是通向成功的唯一道路。
examples.pinyin: Nǔlì shì tōngxiàng chénggōng de wéiyī dàolù.
examples.english: Hard work is the only road leading to success.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.hanzi: 墙上贴着一张电影海报。
example.pinyin: qiáng shàng tiē zhe yì zhāng diànyǐng hǎibào.
example.english: There's a movie poster stuck on the wall.
example.fact: The British government designed the "Keep Calm and Carry On" poster in 1939 to be distributed only if Nazi Germany invaded, so the vast majority of the roughly 2.5 million printed copies were pulped for paper and never displayed. A single surviving copy was rediscovered in a secondhand bookshop in 2000, sparking the design's worldwide popularity decades after it was created.

examples.hanzi: 他们在街上张贴了演唱会的海报。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiē shàng zhāngtiē le yǎnchànghuì de hǎibào.
examples.english: They put up posters for the concert on the street.

examples.hanzi: 我的房间里挂着很多乐队的海报。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān lǐ guà zhe hěn duō yuèduì de hǎibào.
examples.english: My room has many posters of bands hanging in it.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
戈 (spear) — two hands (廾) holding a spear: guarding against danger — hence warn, abstain, and 戒指 ring, from the old sense of guarding.

example.hanzi: 边境部队一直保持高度警戒。
example.pinyin: biānjìng bùduì yìzhí bǎochí gāodù jǐngjiè.
example.english: The border troops remain on high alert at all times.
example.fact: A honeybee colony always keeps a rotating shift of guard bees stationed at the hive entrance, using scent to check whether returning bees belong to the colony before letting them in. Guard bees that detect an intruder release an alarm pheromone that recruits other bees to help repel the threat within seconds.

examples.hanzi: 警察在现场拉起了警戒线。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài xiànchǎng lā qǐ le jǐngjièxiàn.
examples.english: The police put up a cordon at the scene.

examples.hanzi: 台风来临前，沿海地区进入了警戒状态。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, yánhǎi dìqū jìnrù le jǐngjiè zhuàngtài.
examples.english: Before the typhoon, coastal areas went on alert.

components.note: 门 (gate) — marks gates and doors, as in 问, 间, 开; 闪 is a person 人 glimpsed through a gate: a flash, to dodge.
亮 (liàng) is a sound clue for 谅 liàng and 晾 liàng; as a word it means bright, as in 月亮 moon.

example.hanzi: 星星在夜空中闪亮。
example.pinyin: xīngxīng zài yèkōng zhōng shǎnliàng.
example.english: The stars shine brightly in the night sky.
example.fact: Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction between a molecule called luciferin and the enzyme luciferase, converting chemical energy into light with almost no heat lost — a conversion efficiency that puts even LED bulbs to shame. Each firefly species tends to have its own distinct flash pattern, which males and females use to recognize potential mates in the dark.

examples.hanzi: 她的眼睛闪亮着快乐的光芒。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing shǎnliàng zhe kuàilè de guāngmáng.
examples.english: Her eyes sparkled with a joyful light.

examples.hanzi: 舞台上的灯光闪亮，观众都站了起来。
examples.pinyin: Wǔtái shàng de dēngguāng shǎnliàng, guānzhòng dōu zhàn le qǐlái.
examples.english: The stage lights flashed brightly and the audience stood up.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 顺 is a head following the river 川 along.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 顺着这条河往下游走，就能到达大海。
example.pinyin: shùnzhe zhè tiáo hé wǎng xiàyóu zǒu, jiù néng dàodá dàhǎi.
example.english: Follow this river downstream and you'll reach the sea.
example.fact: Salmon famously swim back up the same river system where they were born to spawn, navigating using a combination of the Earth's magnetic field for large-scale orientation and their sense of smell to recognize the precise chemical signature of their home stream once they get close. Some populations travel over 1,000 kilometers upstream against the current to complete the journey.

examples.hanzi: 顺着这条路一直走，就能看到医院。
examples.pinyin: Shùn zhe zhè tiáo lù yīzhí zǒu, jiù néng kàndào yīyuàn.
examples.english: Follow this road straight and you'll see the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 水顺着屋檐流了下来。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ shùn zhe wūyán liú le xiàlái.
examples.english: Water ran down along the eaves.

components.note: 犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — beasts and hunting dogs, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 猎豹的速度让猎物几乎无法逃脱。
example.pinyin: lièbào de sùdù ràng lièwù jīhū wúfǎ táotuō.
example.english: The cheetah's speed leaves its prey almost no chance of escape.
example.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to about 100 km/h in under three seconds and reach top speeds of roughly 100 to 120 km/h, making them the fastest land animal — but they can only sustain that sprint for around 20 to 30 seconds before overheating. Because of this, a hunt usually fails if the prey manages to stay just out of reach that long.

examples.hanzi: 老虎悄悄地接近自己的猎物。
examples.pinyin: Lǎohǔ qiāoqiāo de jiējìn zìjǐ de lièwù.
examples.english: The tiger quietly approached its prey.

examples.hanzi: 猎人带着猎物回到了村子。
examples.pinyin: Lièrén dài zhe lièwù huí dào le cūnzi.
examples.english: The hunter returned to the village with his catch.

components.note: 且 (moreover; once an altar) — the top part. 县 is simplified from 縣, which meant 'to hang'; counties were said to hang directly from the ruler. Origin: traditional account.
厶 (small, private) — the bottom. 县 is also the base of 悬 xuán, 'to hang' (悬挂), which adds a heart 心.

example.hanzi: 我家在一个小县城里。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài yí gè xiǎo xiànchéng lǐ.
example.english: My home is in a small county town.
example.fact: 县 is the administrative unit below prefecture, and 县城 is a county seat. Counties date back over two thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 这个县城离省会不远。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiànchéng lí shěnghuì bù yuǎn.
examples.english: This county town is not far from the provincial capital.

examples.hanzi: 他是县里的老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì xiàn lǐ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: He is a teacher in the county.

meanings: (used in complaining about sth) to be a nuisance

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 今天热得要命。
example.pinyin: jīntiān rè de yàomìng.
example.english: It's unbearably hot today.
example.fact: The highest air temperature ever reliably recorded on Earth's surface was 56.7°C (134°F), measured in Death Valley, California, in July 2013. Death Valley's extreme heat comes partly from its shape: a long, narrow basin below sea level that traps and compresses descending hot air.

examples.hanzi: 我饿得要命，快给我点吃的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ è de yàomìng, kuài gěi wǒ diǎn chī de.
examples.english: I'm starving, so quickly get me something to eat.

examples.hanzi: 这个药苦得要命，我吃不下去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yào kǔ de yàomìng, wǒ chī bù xiàqù.
examples.english: This medicine is terribly bitter and I can't swallow it.
